title: Kendrick Lamar, Billie Eilish, 2Pac & More Soundtrack the West Coast Momentum Mix: Listen Now
summary: Press play on the songs moving the West Coast—built from Luminate data, Billboard editorial expertise, and powered by Planet Fitness
contentText:
The West Coast has always moved to its own rhythm. From the foundational sounds of hip-hop and funk to the genre-blurring artists shaping today’s culture, music across the region reflects confidence, creativity, and constant evolution. The Planet Fitness Movement Mixes explore the songs that become part of those everyday moments — the tracks that fuel workouts, road trips, recovery, and everything in between. 

Curated by Billboard’s editorial team and informed by Luminate’s streaming and consumption data, each playlist reflects real listening behavior — the artists, songs, and sounds people are returning to, replaying, and carrying into their daily routines. It’s where data meets culture: a look at the music that moves communities and defines the energy of a region. 

The West Coast Momentum Mix (listen  HERE ) captures a region where tradition and innovation exist side by side. Built from the top 200 tracks (January 2026–present) across Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Sacramento, and Las Vegas, the playlist reflects the West Coast’s expansive musical identity — from hip-hop and R&B to alternative, rock, pop, and the growing influence of música mexicana. Featuring artists including Kendrick Lamar, Fuerza Regida, Tyler, The Creator, and more, the mix reflects a region that has never been defined by one sound, but by its ability to create what comes next.

From iconic anthems to emerging voices, these are the songs that bring energy to the moments that matter — the ones that keep you moving, one track at a time. 

Code WESTCOASTFMF  gives new members their first month of Planet Fitness membership for FREE and applies to either membership option (Black Card or Classic Card). Offer expires December 31, 2026.

California Love — 2Pac & Dr. Dre
The ultimate West Coast introduction, “California Love” transformed California pride into a global sound. Dr. Dre’s G-funk production — built around bright synths, a deep bassline, and a groove that feels instantly recognizable — created the perfect backdrop for 2Pac’s larger-than-life presence. Released during a pivotal moment in West Coast hip-hop, the track became more than a hit; it became a cultural symbol of ambition, confidence, and the California lifestyle.

Not Like Us — Kendrick Lamar
A modern-day West Coast anthem, “Not Like Us” brought the region’s signature bounce back to the center of popular culture. Kendrick Lamar’s sharp delivery meets Mustard’s unmistakable production style, creating a record that feels rooted in California’s rap history while firmly belonging to the current moment. Its massive chart success, viral impact, and presence across sports, celebrations, and cultural conversations cemented its place as one of the defining hip-hop records of the era.

BABYDOLL — Dominic Fike
Dominic Fike’s “BABYDOLL” represents the genre-fluid sound emerging from today’s California creative scene. Built around breezy guitar melodies, understated percussion, and Fike’s effortlessly melodic delivery, the track carries the relaxed confidence often associated with the West Coast. It reflects a new generation of artists who move freely between indie, pop, and hip-hop, embracing experimentation over traditional boundaries.

No Pole — Don Toliver
Don Toliver’s hypnotic approach to melody and production has become a defining force in modern hip-hop and R&B. “No Pole” leans into atmospheric synths, layered vocals, and a slow-burning groove that feels tailor-made for late-night drives through the city. The track reflects the influence of Los Angeles’ studio culture, where genre lines continue to blur between rap, R&B, and electronic-inspired production.

Folded — Kehlani
Rooted in Kehlani’s Bay Area identity, “Folded” carries forward the West Coast’s long-standing tradition of emotionally driven R&B. The track balances vulnerability with confidence, pairing soulful vocals with polished production that feels contemporary while honoring the region’s rich melodic history. Kehlani’s ability to blend personal storytelling with modern R&B has made her one of the defining voices of the Bay Area’s next generation.

Marlboro Rojo — Fuerza Regida
“Marboro Rojo” represents the evolution of Southern California’s sound, where regional Mexican music continues to expand its influence across mainstream culture. Fuerza Regida’s fusion of traditional instrumentation, modern production, and street-level storytelling reflects the experiences and energy of a new generation of Mexican-American listeners. The group’s rapid rise has helped position música mexicana as one of today’s most influential movements in music.

Can’t Stop — Red Hot Chili Peppers
Few bands are as tied to Los Angeles’ musical identity as the Red Hot Chili Peppers. “Can’t Stop” captures the city’s restless creativity through a fusion of funk, punk, and alternative rock, driven by Flea’s instantly recognizable bassline and the band’s explosive chemistry. A staple across generations, the track embodies the unconventional, genre-blending spirit that has long defined LA’s artistic community.

We Are the People — Empire of the Sun
With sweeping synths, cinematic production, and an almost dreamlike quality, “We Are the People” captures the sense of possibility associated with West Coast exploration. Empire of the Sun’s electronic sound has become closely connected to festival culture, where immersive visuals and expansive production turn songs into shared experiences. The track’s uplifting energy makes it feel built for open roads, outdoor stages, and moments of movement.

Dracula — Tame Impala
Tame Impala’s psychedelic sound has become deeply woven into California’s alternative and festival communities. “Dracula” embraces layered textures, swirling production, and a hypnotic rhythm that reflects the region’s long history of experimental music. It represents the side of the West Coast that thrives on reinvention — where artists continuously reshape genres into something new.

Jump — Van Halen
An essential piece of Southern California rock history, “Jump” helped define the larger-than-life energy of the 1980s Los Angeles music scene. The song’s iconic keyboard riff, explosive guitars, and arena-ready production transformed it into a global anthem. Decades later, it remains a reminder of the ambition and excess that shaped LA’s legendary rock era.

Paradise City — Guns N’ Roses
A defining record from Los Angeles’ legendary rock era, “Paradise City” captures the chaos, ambition, and adrenaline of the Sunset Strip scene. With its massive guitars, unforgettable chorus, and stadium-sized production, the track became a symbol of the rebellious energy surrounding LA rock culture in the late ’80s. It remains one of the most recognizable rock anthems of its generation.

Somebody Told Me — The Killers
While The Killers emerged from Las Vegas, “Somebody Told Me” became part of the broader West Coast alternative soundtrack of the 2000s. The track combines sharp guitar riffs, electronic textures, and an undeniable sense of momentum, reflecting the nightlife and festival energy that shaped the era. Its lasting popularity continues to connect with audiences across generations.

California Gurls — Katy Perry feat. Snoop Dogg
A bright, colorful celebration of California pop culture, “California Gurls” turns the state’s beachside imagery into a global pop moment. Katy Perry’s playful production meets Snoop Dogg’s unmistakable West Coast presence, creating a track that feels synonymous with summer. Its chart success and enduring recognition have made it one of the defining California-inspired pop records of the 2010s.

Hella Good — No Doubt
A high-energy evolution of No Doubt’s Southern California ska-punk roots, “Hella Good” marked the band’s shift toward a more electronic, dance-driven sound. Built around a propulsive bassline, sleek synths, and Gwen Stefani’s commanding vocals, the track blends rock attitude with club-rea…
